title: Bethlehem foretold and remembered
source_text: Εἵρηται δὴ περὶ μὲν τοῦ τόπου τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἀπὸ „Βηθλεὲμ“ „ἐξελεύσεται ὁ ἡγούμενος,“ τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον· „καὶ σὺ Βηθλεὲμ οἶκος τοῦ Ἐφραθὰ, ὀλιγοστὸς εἶ τοῦ εἶναι ἐν χιλιάσιν Ἰούδα· ἐκ σοῦ μοι ἐξελεύσεται τοῦ εἶναι εἰς ἄρχοντα ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ αἱ ἔξοδοι αὐτοῦ ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἐξ ἡμερῶν αἰῶνος.“ αὕτη δ᾿ ἡ προφητεία οὐδενὶ ἁρμόσαι ἂν τῶν, ὥς φησιν ὁ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖος, ἐνθουσιώντων καὶ ἀγειρόντων καὶ λεγόντων ἄνωθεν ἥκειν, ἐὰν μὴ σαφῶς δεικνύηται ἐκ Βηθλεὲμ γεγεννημένος ἢ, ὡς ἂν εἴποι τις ἄλλος, ἀπὸ Βηθλεὲμ ἐπὶ τὸ ἡγεῖσθαι τοῦ λαοῦ ἐρχόμενος. περὶ δὲ τοῦ γεγεννῆσθαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐν Βηθλεὲμ εἰ βούλεταί τις μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Μιχαία προφητείαν καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀναγεγραμμένην ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰησοῦ μαθητῶν ἱστορίαν καὶ ἄλλοθεν πεισθῆναι, κατανοησάτω ὅτι ἀκολούθως τῇ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ περὶ τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἱστορίᾳ δείκνυται τὸ ἐν Βηθλεὲμ σπήλαιον, ἔνθα ἐγεννήθη, καὶ ἡ ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ φάτνη, ἔνθα ἐσπαργανώθη. καὶ τὸ δεικνύμενον τοῦτο διαβόητόν ἐστιν ἐν τοῖς τόποις καὶ παρὰ τοῖς τῆς πίστεως ἀλλοτρίοις, ὡς ἄρα ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ τούτῳ ὁ ὑπὸ Χριστιανῶν προσκυνούμενος καὶ θαυμαζόμενος γεγέννηται Ἰησοῦς. ἐγὼ δ᾿ οἶμαι ὅτι πρὸ μὲν τῆς Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίας οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ γραμματεῖς τοῦ λαοῦ διὰ τὸ σαφὲς καὶ ἐναργὲς τῆς προφητείας ἐδίδασκον ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς ἐν Βηθλεὲμ γεννηθήσεται. καὶ ἔφθανεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς πολλοὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· ὅθεν καὶ ὁ Ἡρώδης ἀναγέγραπται πυνθανόμενος τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων τοῦ λαοῦ ἀκηκοέναι παρ᾿ αὐτῶν ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς „ἐν Βηθλεὲμ τῆς Ἰουδαίας“ γεννηθήσεται, ὅθεν ἦν ὁ Δαυίδ. ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατὰ Ἰωάννην λέλεκται Ἰουδαίους εἰρηκέναι ὅτι ὁ Χριστος ἐν Βηθλεὲμ γεννηθήσεται, ὅθεν ὁ Δαυὶδ ἦν. μετὰ δὲ τὴν Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίαν οἱ πραγματευόμενοι καθελεῖν τὴν περὶ αὐτοῦ ὑπόληψιν ὡς προφητευθέντος ἄνωθεν περὶ τῆς γενέσεως, τὴν τοιαύτην διδασκαλίαν περιεῖλον ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ· ἀδελφόν τι ποιοῦντες τοῖς πείσασι τοὺς ἑωρακότας αὐτὸν ἀναστάντα ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν στρατιώτας τῶν φρουρούντων τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἀπαγγέλλουσιν εἰρηκέναι τοῖς ἰδοῦσιν· „εἴπατε ὅτι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων νυκτὸς ἔκλεψαν αὐτόν. καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.“
pass_a_gloss: It has been said then about the place of his birth that from 'Bethlehem' 'the leader (ἡγούμενος) will come forth', in this manner: 'And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephratha, are least (ὀλιγοστός) to be among the thousands (χιλιάσιν) of Judah; out of you shall come forth for me one to be for ruler (ἄρχοντα) in Israel, and his goings forth (ἔξοδοι) from the beginning, from days of the age (ἐξ ἡμερῶν αἰῶνος).' This prophecy would fit none of those, as the Jew in Celsus says, being in frenzy and begging and saying they come from above, unless he is clearly shown having been born from Bethlehem or, as another might say, coming from Bethlehem to leading (ἡγεῖσθαι) the people. About Jesus having been born in Bethlehem, if one wishes after the prophecy of Micah and after the history recorded in the Gospels by Jesus' disciples to be persuaded also from elsewhere, let him consider (κατανοησάτω) that, consistently with the history in the Gospel about his birth, there is shown (δείκνυται) the cave (σπήλαιον) in Bethlehem where he was born and the manger (φάτνη) in the cave where he was swaddled (ἐσπαργανώθη). And this thing shown is much talked of (διαβόητον) in the places and among those foreign to the faith, that in this cave the Jesus worshipped (προσκυνούμενος) and admired by Christians has been born. I think that before Christ's coming (ἐπιδημία) the chief priests and scribes of the people, through the clearness and vividness (ἐναργές) of the prophecy, taught that the Christ will be born in Bethlehem. And this word reached also the many of the Jews; whence also Herod is recorded, inquiring of the chief priests and scribes of the people, to have heard from them that the Christ will be born 'in Bethlehem of Judea', whence David was. Further also in the [Gospel] according to John it is said that Jews said the Christ will be born in Bethlehem whence David was. After Christ's coming, those busying themselves (πραγματευόμενοι) to pull down (καθελεῖν) the supposition (ὑπόληψις) about him as having been prophesied of old (ἄνωθεν) about his birth removed such teaching from the people, doing something akin (ἀδελφόν) to those who persuaded the soldiers of the guards of the tomb (μνημεῖον), who had seen him risen from the dead and were reporting this, [who are recorded] to have said to those who saw: 'Say that his disciples, we sleeping, by night stole him. And if this be heard before the governor (ἡγεμόνος), we will persuade and make you free of care (ἀμερίμνους).'
pass_b_english: About the place of his birth it has been said that "the ruler will come forth" (Matthew 2:6) from "Bethlehem," in this way: "And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are small indeed to be among the thousands of Judah; out of you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, and his goings forth are from the beginning, from the days of eternity" (Micah 5:2). This prophecy would fit none of those who, as Celsus's Jew says, are in a frenzy and go about begging and say they have come from above, unless he were clearly shown to have been born in Bethlehem, or, as someone else might put it, to have come from Bethlehem to lead the people.

As for Jesus' birth in Bethlehem, if anyone wants to be persuaded from other sources as well, besides Micah's prophecy and the account recorded in the Gospels by Jesus' disciples, let him consider this. In keeping with the Gospel account of his birth, the cave in Bethlehem where he was born is shown, and the manger in the cave where he was wrapped in swaddling cloths (Luke 2:7). And what is shown there is widely known in those parts, even among those who are strangers to the faith: that in this cave was born the Jesus whom Christians worship and admire.

For my part, I think that before Christ's coming the chief priests and scribes of the people taught that the Christ would be born in Bethlehem, because the prophecy was clear and plain. And this teaching reached the mass of the Jews as well. That is why Herod is recorded to have heard from the chief priests and scribes of the people, when he inquired of them, that the Christ would be born "in Bethlehem of Judea" (Matthew 2:4-5), the town David came from. Further, in the Gospel according to John it is said that Jews stated that the Christ would be born in Bethlehem, the town David came from (John 7:42).

But after Christ's coming, those who set to work to destroy the belief that his birth had been foretold long before removed this teaching from the people. In this they did something much like those who won over the soldiers of the guard at the tomb, who had seen him risen from the dead and were reporting it, and who said to those who had seen it: "Say that his disciples stole him by night while we were asleep. And if this is heard before the governor, we will do the persuading and keep you free of trouble" (Matthew 28:13-14).

choices.choice: Micah is quoted from the Septuagint, Micah 5:1 in Hebrew and Greek numbering, 5:2 in English Bibles. The phrase 'the ruler will come forth' (ἐξελεύσεται ὁ ἡγούμενος) is the wording of Matthew 2:6 rather than of Micah, so it is cited to Matthew. 'The town David came from' (ὅθεν ἦν ὁ Δαυίδ) after the Herod episode is Origen's addition, borrowed from John 7:42, which he then cites. Matthew 28:13 is quoted without ἐλθόντες ('came and'), and 28:14 without αὐτόν ('him'); 'we will do the persuading' keeps the object unexpressed. Origen says the soldiers had seen Jesus 'risen from the dead'; Matthew 28:4 and 28:11 say they saw the angel and reported 'all that had happened'; Origen's wording is kept. The construction καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἀπαγγέλλουσιν εἰρηκέναι τοῖς ἰδοῦσιν is loose: the dative participle belongs with the soldiers ('who were reporting it') and εἰρηκέναι depends on an understood 'are recorded'; rendered by sense. The cave and manger at Bethlehem are Origen's own report of what was shown in his day.
Micah 5:2 (LXX 5:1) ὀλιγοστὸς εἶ τοῦ εἶναι: stiff 'are the least to be among' changed to 'are small indeed to be among'
διὰ τὸ σαφὲς καὶ ἐναργές: added intensifier 'so' removed ('because the prophecy was clear and plain')
Ἰουδαίους εἰρηκέναι (no article): 'the Jews stated' changed to 'Jews stated', matching John 7:41-42 where only part of the crowd speaks
Citations checked: Matthew 2:6, Micah 5:2 (LXX numbering converted), Luke 2:7, Matthew 2:4-5, John 7:42, Matthew 28:13-14
